fields.title: Polka: the feed that showed someone else's data
fields.summary: For 40 minutes, the feed was cached without user association: 64 people saw someone else's data.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do today? State the price of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. For 40 minutes after a release, the main screen feed was cached without user association. Some people saw another user's feed: last ordered items, personal recommendations, default store address. The issue was found and fixed. It is now 11 AM, and the question is what comes next.
fields.brief/objective: Resolve the incident honestly and eliminate the class of error rather than just its specific instance.
fields.brief/constraints: The regulatory notification deadline is 72 hours from discovery if the risk is significant.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you are doing today and justify the notification decision.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: The third leak of the same class is fixed by a pipeline, not a test
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A targeted test fixes the specific bug that already happened and says nothing about the next one—and if the root cause is the same, the next one will happen. An automated check in the build pipeline catches an entire class: a cache key without a user identifier simply fails to pass. Meanwhile, the decision to notify is not just a legal one: a small group and an honest explanation are almost always cheaper than a hidden incident coming to light later.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Logs show 64 people saw someone else's feed. Each saw data from one random other user.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: List of recently ordered items (up to 8 positions), default store name, city district. No name, phone number, address, or payment details.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: One: "why do I have someone else's groceries in my app".
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Technically a personal data leak. The threshold for significant risk is debatable. Regulatory notification deadline is 72 hours from discovery if the risk is significant.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Log it, do not notify, add a test
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: One day. Log the incident, add a test for the cache key, do not notify the regulator or users.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: technically permissible if legal counsel interprets the risk as non-significant: no name, phone, or payment details were shown. The test fixes the specific cache key bug. But this is the third incident of the same class in two years, and point fixes have already failed twice. If the story surfaces later—for instance, from the exact person who wrote to support—silence will look worse than a leak.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Notify 64 people, log it, add a test
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Notify 64 people, log it, add a test. Two days.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: honest. A small group, specific explanation. Based on experience with such notifications, the reaction is mostly positive. Notifying the regulator is at the lawyer's discretion.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Notify, plus analyze the problem class: audit all caches for isolation
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: One week. Notify affected users and audit all caches for user data isolation.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: Notification removes reputational risk, and the audit finds other places with the same isolation bug—there are usually several since the root cause is shared. One week of work. What it lacks is a mechanism to catch the next such bug before release: an audit captures today's state, but tomorrow someone will add a new cache.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Notify, audit, plus automated cache key checks in the pipeline
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Notify, audit, plus automated cache key checks in the pipeline. One and a half weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: prevents both current and future issues. Pipeline checks are the same technique used for analytics fields in `SE1-N4-L1` that is already working.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not recognize personal data without direct identifiers
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not know the standard procedure for a data leak
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not see the class of problem behind an individual instance
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Authentication and authorization are not separated when analyzing access
